questions.q: What are the two delivery extensions Reporting Services ships with?
options: E-Mail and Windows File Share
FTP and HTTP POST
SharePoint and OneDrive
SMS and Microsoft Teams
questions.explain: Every subscription hands its rendered report to one of two built-in delivery extensions: E-Mail or Windows File Share.

questions.q: What's the difference between Include Report and Include Link in an e-mail subscription?
options: Include Report embeds or attaches an actual copy of the report; Include Link sends only a URL to it
Include Report sends a PDF only; Include Link sends only Excel files
Include Link is required for file share delivery, not e-mail
There is no difference — both do the same thing
questions.explain: Include Report embeds or attaches the rendered report itself; Include Link just points the recipient to it on the report server. Clearing both leaves only the subject-line notification.

questions.q: What render format should you choose to embed a report directly in the body of an e-mail?
options: MHTML (web archive)
PDF
CSV
HTML 4.0
questions.explain: MHTML embeds the report in the message body; any other render format sends it as an attachment instead.

questions.q: What must already exist before Windows File Share delivery can be used at all?
options: A target shared folder — file share delivery needs no other server-side configuration
An SMTP server configured on the report server
A data-driven subscription dataset
A shared schedule
questions.explain: Unlike e-mail delivery, which must be configured on the report server first, file share delivery just needs a target folder to already exist.

questions.q: What does the file share account setting let a report administrator do?
options: Maintain a single set of credentials centrally, reused by multiple file-share subscriptions
Automatically convert file share deliveries into e-mail deliveries
Encrypt reports before they're written to the share
Bypass the need for a UNC path
questions.explain: The file share account lets an administrator change credentials in one place instead of updating every individual subscription that delivers to a file share.
